en: 1) Religion is one of the most important concerns of our life — as children we were already taught to stammer prayers to the Godhead, our little hands were already folded to raise them to the most exalted being, and a collection of sentences, still unintelligible at the time, was loaded onto our memory, for later use and comfort in our life.
zh: 1）宗教是我们生活里最要紧的事情之一——我们还是孩子的时候，就已经被教着一句一句向神念祷词，小手就被合起来举向那至高者，记忆里也被塞进一堆当时根本不懂的话，为的是日后在生活里用得上、能得安慰。

en: When we grow older, dealings with religion fill a large part of our life; with some people, indeed, the whole circle of their thoughts and inclinations hangs together with religion as the rim of a wheel does with its hub.
Besides other festivals in between, we dedicate to it the first day of every week, which from youth on appears to us in a finer, more festive light than all the other days.

We see around us a particular class of people set apart solely for the service of religion; to all the more important events and actions of human life on which people's private happiness depends — to birth, marriage, death and burial — something religious is mixed in.
zh: 等我们长大一些，跟宗教打交道就占去了我们生活的一大部分；对有些人来说，他们全部的想法和爱好都跟宗教连在一起，就像轮圈连在轮毂上一样。
除了别的节期，我们每个星期的头一天也是献给它的；这一天从少年时起在我们眼里就比别的日子显得更美、更像个节日。
我们身边还看得见专门有一类人，只为服事宗教而设；人生中所有更要紧的事情和举动，凡是私人幸福所系的——出生、婚姻、死亡和下葬——都掺进了宗教的成分。

en: Does a person, when he grows older, reflect on the nature and properties of that being, and especially on the relation of the world to it, to which all his feelings are directed? — Human nature is so constituted that whatever in the doctrine of God is practical, whatever can become a motive for him, a spring of action, a source of the knowledge of his duties and a source of comfort, soon offers itself to an uncorrupted human sense; and the instruction given us about it from youth on, the concepts, all the external things that bear on it and make an impression on us, are of a kind that is grafted onto a natural need of the human spirit — often immediately, but alas all too often only by arbitrary bonds, grounded neither in the nature of the soul nor in the truths that are themselves to be drawn from the concepts and developed out of them. —2)
zh: 人长大以后，会不会去想一想那至高者的本性和属性，特别是世界跟它的关系——他所有的感受都是冲着它去的？——人的天性就是这样安排的：关于神的学说里凡是实际管用的东西，凡是能成为他的动力、变成行动、成为认识义务的源头和安慰的源头的东西，一个没有败坏的常人心思很快就自己碰上了；而从小别人就这件事给我们讲的课、那些概念、一切与此相关并在我们身上留下印象的外在东西，本来就是嫁接在人的精神的一种自然需要上的——这种嫁接常常直接见效，可惜更多时候只是靠一些任意的纽带系上去的，这些纽带既不扎根在灵魂的本性里，也不扎根在那些要从概念本身汲取、从概念本身展开的真理里。——2）

en: … set … of human life in motion.

The exalted demand that reason makes on humanity, whose legitimacy we so often acknowledge with our whole heart when it is fulfilled, and the attractive descriptions that a pure, beautiful imagination has made of innocent or wise people, should never take such hold of us that we hoped to find much of it in the actual world, or believed we could catch and see this beautiful airy image somewhere in reality; discontent with what we find, peevish temper, would then less often cloud our mind.

So let us not be shocked if we must find that sensuousness is the chief element in all human action and striving; how hard it is to distinguish whether mere prudence or real morality is the determining ground of the will.

Satisfaction of the drive to happiness assumed as the highest purpose of life, if only one knows how to calculate well, will outwardly produce just the same effects as when the law of reason determines our will.

As strictly as, in a system of morals, pure morality must be separated in the abstract from sensuousness, and as much as the latter is lowered beneath the former, so much the more must we, in considering man in general and his life, take his sensuousness into account above all — his dependence on outer and inner nature, on what surrounds him and what he lives in, and on sensuous inclinations and blind instinct; human nature is, as it were, only made pregnant with the ideas of reason —: as salt pervades a dish, yet when it is well prepared must nowhere show itself in a lump, but still gives its taste to the whole, or as light pervades and fills everything, shows its influence throughout nature, yet cannot be exhibited as a substance, but still gives objects their shape, breaks differently in each, develops healthful air out of plants — so the ideas of reason enliven the whole fabric of man's feelings, so through their influence action shows itself to him in a light of its own, while they themselves seldom show themselves in their essence, yet their effect pervades everything like a fine matter and gives every inclination and drive a colouring of its own.
zh: ……使人的生活……运转起来。
理性向人类提出的那种崇高要求——它一旦得到满足，我们常常是打心底里承认它正当的——，还有纯洁美好的想象力为无辜的人或智者画出的那些动人图景，都不该把我们抓得那么紧，以至于指望在现实世界里找到许多，或者以为能在什么地方真真切切地抓住、看见这幅美丽的空中楼阁；这样一来，对所见之事的不满、闷闷不乐的脾气，就会少一些蒙住我们的心。
所以，如果我们不得不承认：在人的一切行动和追求里，感性才是最主导的成分，那也不必惊慌；要分辨意志的根据究竟是单纯的精明还是现实的道德，本来就难。
如果把追求幸福的满足当作人生的最高目的，只要算计得够精明，从外表上看，产生的效果跟理性法则决定我们意志时是一样的。

在一套道德学里，纯粹道德必须抽象地跟感性分开，而且分得越干净越好，感性也被压得越低越好；可是在考察一般的人和人的生活时，我们反倒必须特别把人的感性算进去——他对内外自然的依赖，对他周围的环境、他生活在其中的东西的依赖，以及对感性爱好和盲目本能的依赖。人的本性可以说只是被理性的观念受了孕：就像盐能透进一道菜里，做得好的时候哪儿也不该露出一块盐疙瘩，可它还是把味道给了整盘菜；又像光透进一切、充满一切，在自然界处处显出它的作用，却不能作为实体被摆出来，可它仍然给物体以形状，在每个物体里折射得各不相同，还从植物里生出有益健康的空气——理性的观念也是这样，把人的感受这整块织物都激活了，人的行动也因它的作用而显出一种独有的光；观念自己很少以本来的样子露面，但它的作用像一种细微的质料一样浸透一切，给每一种爱好和冲动都染上一种特有的色调。

en: It lies in the concept of religion that it is not a mere science of God, of his properties, of our relation and of the relation of the world to him and of the continuance of our soul — which would at most be acceptable to us either through mere reason or would be known to us in some other way —, not a merely historical or reasoned knowledge, but that it interests the heart, that it has an influence on our feelings and on the determination of our will — in that partly our duties and the laws receive a stronger emphasis from being presented to us as laws of God; partly in that the representation of the sublimity and goodness of God toward us fills our heart with admiration and with feelings of humility and gratitude.
zh: 宗教这个概念本身就含有：它不是单纯关于神、关于神的属性、关于我们同神的关系、世界同神的关系以及我们灵魂长存不灭的学问——这些东西也许要么单凭理性就能让我们接受，要么从别的途径为我们所知——，不是单纯历史性的或推想出来的知识，而是它关涉到心，它对我们的感受、对我们意志的规定有影响——这一方面是因为，我们的义务和法则一经被摆成神的法则，就得到了更强的分量；另一方面是因为，神的崇高和神对我们的善这种表象，让我们的心充满惊叹，充满谦卑和感恩的感受。

en: Religion therefore gives morality and its motives a new, more sublime impetus; it furnishes a new, stronger dam against the violence of sensuous drives.

With sensuous human beings religion too is sensuous — the religious motives to doing good must be sensuous if they are to be able to work on sensuousness; thereby they admittedly usually lose in dignity, insofar as they are moral motives, but thereby they have acquired such a human look, have nestled so closely to our feelings, that we, drawn by our heart and flattered by beautiful imagination, often easily forget that a cold reason disapproves of such image-representations, or even forbids one to want to say anything about them at all.
zh: 所以宗教给道德和道德的动机一种新的、更高的冲劲，也给感性的冲动的暴力筑起一道新的、更坚固的堤坝。
在感性的人那里，宗教也是感性的——要行善的宗教动力必须是感性的，才能对感性起作用；这样一来，它们作为道德的动机，当然通常就失掉了几分尊严，但也因此获得了一副很有人情味的面貌，那么贴近我们的感受，以致我们被自己的心吸引、被美丽的想象力奉承，常常轻易就忘了：冷静的理性并不赞成这类图像式的表象，甚至干脆不许人再想对它说些什么。

en: When one speaks of public religion, one understands by it the concepts of God and immortality and whatever has reference to them, insofar as they make up the conviction of a people, insofar as they have influence on the actions and the way of thinking of that people; further, there also belong here the means by which these ideas are partly taught to the people, partly made pressing on the heart; under this effect is not merely the immediate one understood, that I do not steal because God forbade it — especially the more remote ones must be taken into account, and are often to be valued as the most important.

These are mainly the elevation, the ennoblement of the spirit of a nation, that the feeling of its dignity, so often slumbering, be awakened in its soul, that the people does not throw itself away and does not let itself be thrown away, that it feels itself not only as human beings, but that also gentler tints of humanity and goodness be brought into the picture.
zh: 说到公共宗教，人们指的是关于神和不死的概念，以及与此相关的东西，只要它们构成一个民族的信念，只要它们对这个民族的行动和想法有影响；此外，这里还包括那些手段：靠这些手段，这些观念一部分被教给民众，一部分被送进他们的心里去；这里说的作用，不只是直接的那一种，即我不偷窃是因为神禁止过——尤其是那些较远的作用必须算进来，而且往往要估得最重要。
这些作用主要是提升、是使一个民族的精神变得高尚，是把那个常常沉睡着的尊严感在它心里唤醒，是让这个民族不糟践自己、也不让人糟践自己，是让它不只感到自己是人，而且还让人性与善良的、更柔和的色调被添进这幅画里。

en: The main doctrines of the Christian religion have presumably remained the same since their origin, but according to the circumstances of the time, the one doctrine was quite pushed into the shadow and another was chiefly raised up, brought into the light and twisted at the expense of the darkened one, either extended too far or restricted too much.
zh: 基督宗教的主要教义自产生以来大概一直是同一套，但随时代情况的不同，这一条教义被完全推进阴影里，另一条则被特别抬举、被放到光下，并且以被遮暗的那条为代价而被扭曲，要么被撑得太开，要么被收得太紧。

en: The whole mass of religious principles and of the feelings flowing from them, and especially the degree of strength with which they can flow into the manner of acting, is the main point of a folk religion.
On an oppressed spirit that has lost its youthful strength under the burden of its chains and begins to age, religious ideas can make little impression.
zh: 全部宗教原则以及由它们流出来的感受，尤其是它们能带着多大的力量流进行动方式里去，这才是民间宗教的要点。
一个受压迫的精神，在锁链的重压下已经失去了年轻的力量、开始变老，宗教观念在它身上起不了多少作用。

en: The youthful genius of a people — [the] aging one: the former feels itself and exults in its strength, flies with ravenous hunger at something new, takes the liveliest interest in it, but perhaps leaves it again and seizes something else, yet this can never be something that would want to lay fetters on its proud free neck; the aging genius is distinguished above all by firm attachment to what is traditional in every respect, bears therefore the fetters as an old man bears the gout, at which he grumbles but which he cannot get rid of, lets himself be pushed and shaken as his ruler wants, enjoys however only with half consciousness, not freely, not openly, with a cheerful, beautiful joy that invites others to sympathy — its festivals are chatter, as for an old man nothing goes above chatting, not a full resounding cry, not full-blooded enjoyment.
zh: 一个民族的年轻天才——〔还有〕那个衰老的天才：前者感到自己，在自己的力量里欢呼，带着饿狼般的饥渴扑向新东西，对它兴趣最浓，但也许又把它丢开，去抓别的，可这别的永远不可能是想给它高傲自由的脖子套上枷锁的东西；衰老的天才则首先以对一切成规旧习的牢固依恋为标志，因此他戴着枷锁，就像老人带着痛风，一边抱怨，一边又甩不掉，任人推搡摇撼，全凭他的统治者高兴，享受的时候却只带着一半意识，不自由，不敞开，不是那种能引来别人同感的明朗美好的快乐——他的节庆就是闲扯，就像老人没了闲聊就过不去，不是齐声的欢呼，不是热血充盈的享受。

15.en: Exposition of the difference between objective and subjective religion; importance of this exposition with regard to the whole question.
15.zh: 客观宗教与主观宗教之区别的阐明；就整个问题而言这一阐明的重要性。

en: Objective religion is fides quae creditur; the understanding and the memory are the powers that work in it, that investigate, think through and retain the cognitions, or also believe them.

Practical cognitions can also belong to objective religion, but insofar they are only a dead capital — objective religion can be ordered in the head, it can be brought into a system, presented in a book and expounded to others through speech; subjective religion expresses itself only in feelings and actions —: if I say of a human being that he has religion, that does not mean he has great cognitions of it, but it means his heart feels the deeds, the wonders, the nearness of the Godhead, it recognizes, it sees God in its nature, in the fates of human beings, he throws himself down before him, thanks him and praises him in his deeds, in his action looks not merely at whether it is good or prudent, but also the thought: it is well-pleasing to God, is a motive for it — often the strongest; in enjoyment, in a happy event he at the same time directs a glance at God and thanks him for it. — Subjective religion is living, efficacy in the interior of the essence and activity outward.

Subjective religion is something individual, objective [religion] the abstraction; the former the living book of nature, the plants, insects, birds and animals, as they live among one another, one from the other, each lives, each enjoys, they are mixed together, everywhere one finds all kinds together — the latter the cabinet of the teacher of nature, who has killed the insects, dried the plants, stuffed the animals or keeps them in brandy and ranges everything together that nature separated, orders it only according to one purpose, whereas nature intertwined an infinite multiplicity of purposes into a friendly bond.
zh: 客观宗教是 fides quae creditur（被信的信），在其中起作用的力量是知性和记忆，它们去探究、思考并保存这些知识，或者也去相信它们。

客观宗教里也可以有实践性的知识，但就这方面说，它们只是一笔死资本——客观宗教可以在头脑里整理，可以被编成一个体系，写在一本书里，靠讲话讲给别人听；主观宗教却只在感受和行动中表现出来——：如果我说一个人有宗教，这并不是说他对宗教有很多知识，而是说他的心感受到神的作为、奇迹和神的临近，它认识，它在自然中、在人的命运中看见神，他在神面前俯下身去，感谢神，在神的作为中赞美神，他做一件事时，不只看它是否善、是否精明，而且还想到：这是神所喜悦的，这个念头对这件事来说就是一个动机——往往是最强的动机；在享受的时候，在遇到一件幸事的时候，他同时也向神投去一瞥，为此感谢神。——主观宗教是活的，是本质内部的起作用，是向外的活动。
主观宗教是个别的东西，客观宗教则是抽象；前者是自然的活书，是植物、昆虫、鸟和兽，它们彼此之间靠对方活着，每一个都活着，每一个都在享受，它们混在一起，到处都能见到各种类聚在一处；——后者是自然老师的标本柜，他把昆虫弄死，把植物烘干，把动物做成标本或者泡在烧酒里，并且把自然分开的东西统统排列在一起，只按一个目的来整理，而自然本来是把无穷多的目的缠成一条友好的纽带。

en: The whole mass of religious cognitions that belong to objective religion can be the same among a great people, it could in itself be the same over the whole earth; it is interwoven into subjective religion, but makes up only a small, rather ineffective part of it, modifies itself differently in every human being; the most important thing that comes into consideration in subjective religion is whether and how far the mind is disposed to let itself be determined by religious motives, how great its excitability for them is; and then which kinds of representations above all make an impression on the heart, which kinds of feelings are most cultivated in the soul and most easily brought forth — the one human being has no sense for the gentler representations of love, motives taken from the love of God do not strike his heart, his coarser organs of feeling are stirred only by the excitation of fear, by thunder and lightning, the strings of his heart do not resound to the gentle touch of love; other ears are deaf to the voice of duty, it is of no use to draw their attention to the inner judge of actions, who has set up his seat in the heart of the human being himself, to conscience — in them this voice has never sounded; self-interest is the pendulum whose swings keep their machine going.
zh: 属于客观宗教的全部宗教知识，在一个大民族那里可以是同一套，它本身在整块大地上都可以是同一套；它编织在主观宗教里，但只构成其中很小、相当不起作用的一部分，而且在每个人身上都变得不一样；在主观宗教里最要紧的一点是：心是否愿意、在多大程度上愿意让宗教的动机来规定自己，它对这些动机的敏感有多大；其次是什么样的表象最能打动人心，什么样的感受在灵魂里培植得最多、最容易引发出来——有的人对爱那些较柔和的表象毫无感觉，从神的爱中取来的动机敲不开他的心，他那些粗糙的感受器官只有靠唤起恐惧、靠雷鸣电闪才被摇醒，他心上的弦不会应和爱的轻柔弹拨；另一些耳朵对义务的声音是聋的，提醒他们注意行为的内在裁判者、注意良心，是没用的——那个裁判者把座位设在人自己的心里——在他们那里，这个声音从来没有响过；自私自利是那只钟摆，它的摆动让他们的机器保持运转。

en: On this disposition, on this receptivity, it depends how subjective religion is to be constituted in each individual.

Objective religion is taught to us from youth on in the schools; early enough one loads it upon our memory, so that often the understanding, not yet grown strong, the beautiful tender plant of the open free sense, is pressed down under the burden; or as roots work their way through a loose soil and entwine themselves with it and suck their nourishment from it, but are bent aside by a stone and seek another direction, so the burden laid upon memory remains lying undissolved; the soul-powers that have grown strong either shake it off entirely or let it lie on one side and draw no nourishing sap from it.
zh: 主观宗教在每一个个人身上应该是什么样子，就取决于这种心情，取决于这种接受能力。
客观宗教我们从少年时起就在学校里被教；人们够早就把它压到我们的记忆上，以致那还没有长壮的知性、那坦率自由的心意这株美好娇嫩的植物，常常被压在重担底下；或者就像根须在松软的土里穿行，和土缠在一起，从土里吸取养分，却被一块石头顶偏了，只好另找出路一样，加在记忆上的重担也就一直搁着，没有化解，长壮了的灵魂力量要么把它整个甩掉，要么就把它丢在一边，不从里面吸取任何滋养的汁液。

en: Into every human being nature has sunk a seed of the finer feelings that arise out of morality, it has laid in him a sense for the moral, for purposes wider than mere sensuousness; that these beautiful seeds do not smother, that out of them a real receptivity for moral ideas and feelings arise, this is the business of upbringing, of education.
Religion is not the first thing that can take root in the mind; it must meet with a tilled soil in which it can first thrive.
zh: 自然在每个人心里都埋下了一颗更精细的感受的种子，这些感受是从道德里长出来的；它也在人心里放了一种对道德的东西、对超出单纯感性的更远大目的的感觉；这些美好的种子不要被闷死，要从中长出对道德观念和道德感受的现实接受能力，这是教育、是教养的事。
宗教不是心里头一个能扎根的东西，它必须遇到一块已经耕过的地，才能在上面长起来。

en: Everything depends on subjective religion; this has a proper, true worth — the theologians may quarrel about the dogmas, about what belongs to objective religion, about the closer determinations of these propositions; every religion has at its basis a few fundamental propositions, which are only more or less modified, disfigured, more or less purely presented in the different religions — which make up the ground of all faith, of all hopes that religion hands to us.

When I speak of religion, I abstract absolutely from all scientific or rather metaphysical cognition of God, of our relation and that of the whole world to him, etc. Such a cognition, in which merely the reasoning understanding is occupied, is theology, no longer religion.
I count cognitions of God and immortality as belonging to religion only insofar as the need of practical reason demands, and what stands in an easily surveyed connection with it.
Thereby closer explanations about particular arrangements of God for the best of human beings are not excluded.
zh: 一切都取决于主观宗教，它才有真正的价值——神学家们尽可以去争论教义，争论属于客观宗教的东西，争论这些命题更细致的规定；每一种宗教的底子上都只有少数几条基本原理，它们在不同的宗教里只是被或多或少地改动、走样，被或多或少纯粹地表述出来——它们构成一切信仰、构成宗教交到我们手上的一切希望的根据。
我说宗教时，是干脆撇开一切关于神、关于我们和整个世界同神的关系等等的科学认识，或者不如说形而上学认识。这样一种认识只让推想的知性去忙，它是神学，不再是宗教。
我在这里只把实践理性的需要所要求的那部分关于神和不死的知识算作宗教，以及同它处在一种容易看出的联系里的东西。
这样，关于神为了人的好处所作的特别安排，更详细的说明并不被排除在外。

en: But I speak of objective religion too only insofar as it makes up a component of the subjective.
zh: 不过，我谈到客观宗教，也只是就它构成主观宗教的一个组成部分而言。

en: My intention is not to investigate which religious doctrines have the most interest for the heart, can give the soul the most comfort and elevation; not how the doctrines of a religion must be constituted that is to make a people better and happier, but what arrangements belong to this, that the doctrines and the power of religion be mixed into the fabric of human feelings, be joined to their motives to action and prove themselves living and effective in them — that it become wholly subjective; when it is that, it does not express its existence merely through folded hands, through bending of knees and heart before the holy, but it spreads over all branches of human inclinations (without the soul being precisely conscious of it) and works along everywhere, but only mediately — it works, to express myself thus, negatively, in the cheerful enjoyment of human joys or in the performance of sublime deeds and the exercise of the gentler virtues of human love; even if it does not work immediately, it still has the finer influence that it at least lets the soul continue working freely and openly and does not paralyse the sinews of its activity; — to the expression of human powers, be it of courage, of humanity, as to being glad, to the enjoyment of life, there belongs freedom from a malignant disposition of the soul to envy and the like, there belongs innocence, a pure conscience, and these two qualities religion helps to promote.

Thus it also has influence in that innocence, connected with it, knows how to hit exactly the point where being glad would degenerate into excess, courage and resoluteness into encroachment on the rights of others.
zh: 我的目的不是去考察哪些宗教教义最能引起心的兴趣、最能给灵魂安慰和提升；也不是去考察一种要把一个民族变得更好更幸福的宗教，它的教义必须是什么样子；而是要考察，需要一些什么样的安排，才能使宗教的教义和力量掺进人的感受这块织物里，加入人行动的动力之中，并在其中显得有生命、起作用——使它完全成为主观的；当它成为主观的，它表现自己的存在，就不只是靠合掌、靠向神圣者屈膝屈心，而是散布到人的一切爱好上去（灵魂自己并不一定意识到），到处都跟着起作用，但只是间接地起作用——它起的作用，用我的话来说，是消极的：在人欢欢喜喜享受人生乐趣的时候，或者在做出崇高的事情、练习人类之爱那些较柔和的德性的时候；即使它不直接起作用，它也还有那更细致的影响，就是至少让灵魂在这件事上有自由、敞开着继续做下去，不把灵魂活动的筋腱弄瘫；——要发挥人的力量，不论是勇气还是人情，要高兴，要享受生活，都需要灵魂摆脱嫉妒之类的恶劣心情，需要无辜、清白的良心，而这两种品性，宗教都能帮着促成。
它也有这样的影响：与它相连的无辜，能恰好找到那个点，在那里，高兴会变成放纵，勇气和果断会变成侵犯别人的权利。

en: If theology is a matter of the understanding and of memory — its origin may otherwise be wherever it will, out of religion itself —, but religion a matter of the heart, interesting because of a need of practical reason, then it is self-evident that different soul-powers are effective in religion and theology and that different preparations of the mind are also required for both.

In order to be able to hope that the highest good, one component of which it is laid upon us as a duty to make real, become real as a whole, practical reason demands faith in a Godhead — in immortality.
zh: 如果神学是知性和记忆的事——它的来源随它在哪儿，哪怕就出自宗教本身——，而宗教是心的事，是因实践理性的需要而让人关心的，那么不言自明：在宗教和神学里起作用的是不同的灵魂力量，为两者所需要的心的准备也不一样。
为了能够希望那至善——把它的一个组成部分变成现实，是我们的义务——在整体上成为现实，实践理性要求信仰一个神——信仰不死。

en: This is at least the germ from which religion springs — and conscience, the inner sense for right and wrong, and the feeling that punishment must follow wrongdoing and happiness right-doing, is in this deduction of religion only dissolved into its component parts, into distinct concepts.

Whether the idea of a mighty invisible being came into the human soul through some terrible natural phenomenon, or whether God first revealed himself to men in the thunderstorm, where everyone feels the presence of God more closely, or in the gentle whispering of the evening wind, it met with that moral feeling which found that idea entirely suited to its need.
zh: 这至少是宗教由之萌发的种子，——而良心、对是非的内在感觉，以及认为做错事必跟着惩罚、做对事必跟着幸福的那种感受，在这番对宗教的推演中，只是被分解成它的各个组成部分，分解成清晰的概念。
一个强大而不可见的存在者的观念，也许是靠某种可怕的自然现象进入人的灵魂的，也许神最初是在雷雨中向人显现的——那时每个人都更近地感到神的在场——或者是在晚风轻柔的吹拂中显现的，不管怎样，它都碰上了那种道德感受，而这种感受觉得那个观念完全合乎自己的需要。

en: Religion is mere superstition when one takes from it grounds for determining action in those cases where only prudence should give advice, or when fear of the Godhead performs certain actions by which one believes one can avert its displeasure.

Among many sensuous peoples religion is indeed of such a kind — the representation of God and of his way of acting toward men confines itself to this, that he acts according to the laws of human sensuousness and only upon their sensuousness, and very little that is moral is mixed into this concept. — The concept of God, and of turning to him (service), is already more moral, that is, it already points more to a consciousness of a higher order determined by greater purposes than sensuous ones — even if the superstition touched on above is also mixed in, yet along with the inquiry to the Godhead about the future, about the success of an undertaking, there is also joined the invocation of its assistance, the feeling that everything depends on its decisions, and everywhere the belief lies at the bottom, or at least exists alongside the belief in fate and natural necessity, that it dispenses happiness only to the righteous, but brings misfortune upon the unrighteous and the arrogant — and if moral motives for acting are drawn from religion.
zh: 在只有精明才该出主意的场合，人却从宗教里取来行动的根据，或者由于对神的畏惧而做出某些行为、以为借此就能消除神的不满，——这时宗教就只是迷信。

在许多感性的民族那里，宗教大概就是这样一种情形——关于神、以及关于神如何对待人的表象，仅限于这一点：他按人的感性的规律起作用，并且只作用于人的感性，掺进这个概念里的道德成分少得可怜。——关于神、以及关于向神求助（事奉）的概念，已经比较道德了，也就是说，它已经更多地指向一种更高的秩序的意识，这种秩序是由比感性更大的目的规定的，——即使上面提到的迷信也掺了进来，但在向神询问未来、询问一桩事业能否成功的同时，也伴随着祈求神的帮助，伴随着一切都取决于神的决断的那种感受，而且到处都以这种信仰为基础，或者至少在对命运、对自然必然性的信仰之外还有这种信仰：神只把幸福赐给正义的人，却把灾祸降给不义的人和骄横的人，——并且如果人们从宗教里取来行动的道德动机的话。

en: Subjective religion is with good men — the objective kind may have almost any colour it likes — pretty much the same; what makes me a Christian for you, that makes you a Jew for me, says Nathan — for religion is a matter of the heart, which often acts inconsistently against the dogmas that its understanding or memory accepts; the most worthy of reverence among men are certainly not always those who have speculated most about religion, who very often turn their religion into theology, that is, often exchange fullness and warmth of faith for cold cognitions and parades of words.
zh: 主观的宗教在好人那里——客观的宗教几乎想是什么颜色就是什么颜色——差不多是一样的：使我成为你们眼中的基督徒的，也使你们成为我眼中的犹太人，纳坦这样说——因为宗教是心的事情，而心常常跟它的知性或记忆所接受的教条不一致地行事；最值得敬重的人肯定并不总是对宗教思辨得最多的那些人，他们往往把自己的宗教变成神学，也就是说，常常拿冷冰冰的认识和词句的排场，换掉信仰的充实和热忱。

en: But religion gains very little through the understanding; on the contrary, its operations, its doubts, can cool the heart more than warm it; and whoever has found that the ways of representing things of other nations, or of the heathens as they are called, contain much that is absurd, and who therefore rejoices mightily in his higher insights, in his understanding, which he lets see further than the greatest men saw, does not know the essence of religion.

He who calls his Jehovah Jupiter or Brahma and is a true worshipper of God brings his thanks and his sacrifice just as childlike as the true Christian. — Whom does that beautiful simplicity not move, when innocence, amid the good things that nature offers it, thinks of its greatest benefactor, offers him the best, the most spotless, the firstlings of the corn and of the sheep — who does not admire Coriolanus, when in the greatness of his fortune, fearing Nemesis, just as Gustavus Adolphus humbled himself before God at the battle of Lützen, he asks the gods to humble not the genius of Roman greatness but himself.
zh: 可是宗教通过知性所得甚少，知性的运作、知性的怀疑反倒会让心变冷而不是变暖；谁要是发现别的民族、或者所谓的异教徒的表象方式里有许多荒谬的东西，并因此对自己更高的洞见、对自己那个被允许看得比最伟大的人物还远的知性大为高兴，谁就不懂得宗教的本质。

一个人把自己的耶和华称作朱庇特或梵天，同时又是真正的敬神者，那么他就会跟真正的基督徒一样，同样孩子气地献上自己的感谢、自己的祭品。——当无辜的人在自然拿给她的好处当中想到自己最大的恩人，把最好、最无瑕的东西，把谷物和羊群的初熟之物献给他时，谁不为这种美好的纯朴所触动呢——当科里奥兰在好运的顶峰，由于畏惧复仇女神，就像古斯塔夫·阿道夫在吕岑会战中在神面前谦卑下来那样，请求诸神不要使罗马伟大的天才谦卑、而要使他本人谦卑时，谁不佩服他呢。

en: Traits of this kind are for the heart and want to be enjoyed with the heart, with simplicity of spirit and of feeling, not to be carped at with the cold understanding. — Only the self-conceit of the sectarian spirit, which thinks itself wiser than all men of other parties, can, at the innocent last will of Socrates — to bring a cock to the god of health — let the beautiful feeling of Socrates pass by unenjoyed, namely that he thanks the gods for his death, which he regards as recovery, and make the spiteful remark that Tertullian makes, Apologeticum ch. 46 — Socrates etc.
zh: 这一类特征是说给心的，要用心的、要用精神和感受的纯朴去领受，而不是用冷冰冰的知性去挑剔。——只有宗派精神的自负，那种自以为比别的派别的一切人都聪明的自负，才会在苏格拉底那个天真的遗愿面前——向健康之神献一只公鸡——对苏格拉底美好的感受，也就是他为自己视作康复的死亡而感谢诸神，毫无体会地放过，还要作出德尔图良在《护教篇》第46章所作的那种恶意的评注——苏格拉底等等。

en: Where the heart, as with the lay brother in the scene in Nathan from which the above words are taken, does not speak more purely than the understanding, when it stays shut and gives the latter time to reason about an action — that heart is already not worth much, love does not dwell in it.

Nowhere are the voice of uncorrupted feeling, of the pure heart, and the obstinate claim to be right of the understanding more beautifully set against each other than in the story in the Gospel, where Jesus accepted from a woman once of ill repute the anointing of his body — as the open outpouring, not to be led astray by the company standing around, of a beautiful soul filled with repentance, trust and love — with pleasure and love, whereas some of his apostles had too cold a heart to feel along with the depth of this womanly feeling, her beautiful sacrifice of trust, and could make the cold marginal gloss trimmed with the pretext of an interest in charity. — What a bare and forced remark it is when good Gellert says somewhere that a small child nowadays knows more about God than the wisest heathen, just as Tertullian, Apologeticum ch. 46, deum quilibet opifex etc. Just as if the compendium of morals that I have standing here in my cupboard, and which is at my disposal only insofar as it depends on me whether I want to use it for the wrapping of a stinking cheese, had more value than the perhaps at times unjust heart of a Frederick II.; for the difference between the opifex of Tertullian, the child of Gellert into whom the theological leaven has been beaten along with the catechism, and the paper on which morals have been printed, is on the whole in this respect not very great — consciousness actually acquired through experience is missing in both in almost equal degree.
zh: 在上面那些话所取材的《纳坦》那一场里，如果一个人不像那个修道院修士那样，让心比知性说得更纯粹，而是把心闭锁起来，让知性有时间去对一桩行为说长道短，——那么这颗心就已经不怎么样了，爱并不住在它里面。

在福音书里的那个故事中，未受败坏的感受的声音、纯洁的心的声音，与知性的自以为是，从没有对照得比那里更美：耶稣在那里从一个曾经声名不好的女人手里领受了为他抹身这件事——把它看作一颗充满悔恨、信赖和爱心的美好灵魂坦然的倾吐，并不因为围在四周的人而慌乱——以喜悦和爱接受了它；但他的一些门徒心肠太冷，体会不出这种女性感受的深沉，体会不出她这份信赖的美好献礼，还能作出那种冷冰冰的、拿关心贫苦作借口镶上边的旁批。——当善良的盖勒特在某处说，如今一个小孩子对神的了解也比最聪明的异教徒多，就像德尔图良《护教篇》第46章说的 deum quilibet opifex 等等，这是多么干瘪而生硬的一句评语。简直就像我这儿柜子里摆着的那本道德提要——它是否归我支配，只看我愿不愿意拿它去包一块发臭的奶酪——比一个腓特烈二世也许有时并不公正的心更有价值似的；因为德尔图良的 opifex、盖勒特那个连教义问答一起把神学的酵打进去的孩子，同印上道德学说的那张纸之间的区别，总的说来在这方面并不很大——真正靠经验得来的意识，两者差不多同样地缺乏。

31.en: Enlightenment — Wanting to Work through the Understanding
31.zh: 启蒙——想靠知性发挥作用

en: The understanding serves only objective religion. — [It serves] to purify the principles, to present them in their purity — it has brought forth glorious fruits, [e.g.] Lessing's Nathan, and deserves the eulogies with which one always exalts it.
zh: 知性只服务于客观的宗教。——[它的用处在于]把原则澄清，把它们在其纯粹性中呈现出来——它结出了美好的果实，[例如]莱辛的《纳坦》，它配得上人们一向加给它的那些颂词。

en: But through the understanding the principles are never made practical.
zh: 可是靠知性，原则永远也落不到实践里。

en: The understanding is a courtier who obligingly conforms to the moods of his master — it knows how to hunt up justifying grounds for every passion, for every undertaking; it is above all a servant of self-love, which is always very sharp-witted at giving a fine colour to the faults committed or about to be committed, and often praises itself for having found such a good pretext for itself.
zh: 知性是个宫廷侍臣，殷勤地顺着主人的脾气转——它懂得为每一种情欲、每一桩事业找出辩护的理由；它尤其是自爱的仆人，而自爱总是十分机敏，能给已经犯下或就要犯下的过失涂上一层好看的色彩，还常常自我夸耀，说自己找到了一个多好的借口。

en: Enlightenment of the understanding indeed makes one cleverer, but not better.

Even if one traces virtue back to prudence, even if one reckons up to a man that without virtue he cannot become happy, the calculation is far too subtle and too cold to be effective in the moment of action, to have any influence on life at all.
zh: 知性的启蒙固然使人更精明，却不使人更好。
就算人们把美德归结为精明，就算向人算清楚：没有美德他就不能得到幸福，这笔账也还是太精细、太冷，不可能在行动的那一刻起作用，根本不可能对生活有什么影响。

en: If a man takes up the best moral teaching and makes himself acquainted with the most precise determinations, both about the general principles and about the individual duties and virtues, and if one wanted to think of this heap of rules and exceptions in actual action, there would come out such a twisted way of acting, which would be eternally anxious and at strife with itself.

Who that has ever written a moral teaching would himself ever hope that there would be a man who should either learn the book by heart, or, in everything he does, with every inclination that comes over him, look up his moral teaching to see whether it is also moral, whether it is permitted.
And yet this is actually the demand that one makes of a man with a moral teaching.

That bad inclinations do not arise at all, that they do not reach a great height — no printed moral teaching, no enlightenment of the understanding can achieve this; this negative effect [is what] Campe's Theophron [aims at] — [not:] man should act himself, work himself, resolve for himself, not let others act for him, [but rather he] is there nothing more than a mere machine.
zh: 谁要是拿起最好的一部道德学说，把普遍原则以及个别义务和美德的最精确规定都弄清楚，而人在现实行动时又想去想这一大堆规则和例外，那就会弄出这样一种别扭的行动方式：永远提心吊胆，自己跟自己打架。
哪一个写过道德学说的人，会自己希望真有这样一个人：他要么把这本书背下来，要么在每件事上、在每一种袭上心来的倾向面前，都去翻查自己的道德学说，看它是否合乎伦理、是否被允许。
可这恰恰就是人们拿一部道德学说向人提出的要求。
恶劣的倾向根本不冒出来，不发展到很高的程度，——这是任何印出来的道德学说、任何知性的启蒙都做不到的；这种消极的效果[正是]坎佩的《忒俄弗龙》[所追求的]——[不是:]人应当自己行动、自己发挥作用、自己下决心，而不是让别人替自己行动，[而是他]在那里不过是一台纯粹的机器。

en: When one speaks of enlightening a people, this presupposes that errors rule among them, popular prejudices relating to religion — and most of them are more or less of this character, they are grounded in sensuousness, in the blind expectation that an effect will follow which stands in no connection at all with the cause by which the effect is supposed to be produced; among the people that has many prejudices, the concept of cause seems mostly still to be grounded on the concept of mere succession, in that they [not] seldom, even where they speak of causes, omit the middle members of the successive effects and do not see. — Sensuousness and imagination are the sources of prejudices; even correct propositions that stand up to the examination of the understanding are, among the common people, also prejudices insofar as they only believe them, since they know no grounds for them.
zh: 当人们说要启蒙一个民族时，这就预设了这个民族中间流行着谬误，即与宗教有关的民众偏见，——而大多数偏见或多或少都属于这种性质，它们立足于感性，立足于一种盲目的期待：以为会有某种效果出现，而它和应当产生这效果的原因根本毫无关联；在一个有许多偏见的民族那里，原因这个概念多半还建立在单纯的先后相继这个概念上，因为他们即使在谈到原因时，也[不]少见地略去那些相继出现的中间环节，看不明白。——感性和想象力是偏见的来源；就连正确的、经得起知性考察的命题，在普通人那里也是偏见，因为他们只是相信它，并不知道它的根据。

en: Prejudices can therefore be of two kinds
zh: 所以偏见可以有两种

en: a) real errors,
zh: a) 现实的谬误，

en: b) real truths, which however are not to be seen as truths, recognised as such through reason, but are acknowledged on trust and faith — and in which therefore subjectively no greater merit takes place.
zh: b) 现实的真理，但它们不是要被当作真理看出来、由理性认其为真理，而是凭忠信和信仰被承认——因此在这里，主观上并没有什么更大的功劳。

en: To take away a people's prejudices, to enlighten it, thus means — for prejudices of a practical kind, that is, those that have influence on the determination of the will, have quite different sources and different consequences, and of these there is no talk here — it means to cultivate its understanding with regard to certain objects in such a way that it on the one hand really tears itself away from conviction and the violence of errors, and on the other is convinced of the real truths through grounds.
But first of all, what mortal wants to decide at all what truth is?

But let us here assume, as it must be if one speaks of human knowledge more in concreto, and as one must also assume merely in a political respect if human society is to take place, that there are universally valid principles which are not only evident to sound human understanding, but must also lie at the basis of every religion if it is to deserve this name, however disfigured they may be —
zh: 所以，去掉一个民族的偏见、启蒙它，意思是——因为实践类的偏见，也就是对意志的规定有影响的那种偏见，来源完全不同，后果也不同，这里不谈它们——意思是把它在涉及某些对象时的知性培养成这样：一方面它真正从对谬误的信服和谬误的势力中挣脱出来，另一方面它凭理由对现实的真理确信不疑。
但首先，哪一个会死的人愿意来断定什么是真理呢？
但我们在这里不妨假定——如果更具体地谈论人的知识，就必定要这样假定，而且只要人类社会要存在，哪怕仅从政治方面看也必须这样假定——存在着普遍有效的原则，它们不仅对健全的人类知性是不言而喻的，而且必定也是每一种宗教的基础，只要这种宗教配得上宗教这个名称，不管它被歪曲成什么样子，——

en: α) so it is certain that of them there are only few, and that precisely for that reason — because they are in part so general and abstract, in part, when they are to be presented purely, as reason demands, [contradict] experience and sensuous semblance, since they are not a rule for these but can only fit a contrary order of things — they do not easily qualify for a living recognition on the part of the people; and even if memory has retained them, they still do not make up any part of man's spiritual, desiring system;
zh: α) 所以可以肯定，这样的东西只有少数几条；而且正因为它们一部分如此普遍而抽象，一部分在要按理性的要求被纯粹地表述出来时，[违背]经验和感性假象——因为它们并不是经验和假象的规则，只能适用于一种与之相反的物的秩序——所以它们不容易得到人民活生生的认可；即使记忆把它们保留了下来，它们也还不构成人的精神的、欲求的系统的一部分；

en: β) since it is impossible that a religion which is to be universally for the people can consist of general truths, to which at every time only more distinguished men have attained and which they embraced with love and their whole heart, and thus in part additions must always be mixed in that must simply be accepted on trust and faith, or the purer propositions must be coarsened and put into a more sensuous husk, if they are to be understood and agreeable to sensuousness, and in part such usages must be introduced, of whose necessity or usefulness a confiding faith or habituation from youth on must also persuade one10) — so it is clear that folk religion, and (what is already bound up with the concept of religion as such) if its doctrines are to be effective in life and deed, can impossibly be built on mere reason. - Positive religion rests necessarily on belief in the tradition through which it is handed down to us, - and thus we can be convinced of the obligation to its religious usages, of the belief that God demands them of us as well-pleasing, as duty, only through this ground.

But considered in itself merely with reason, no more can be asserted of them than that they serve for edification, for the awakening of pious feelings, and their appropriateness for this can be examined.

But as soon as I have convinced myself that God is not honoured in himself by these usages, by our service, that doing right is the most well-pleasing service to him, yet that I still see that these usages serve for edification, then precisely through this these usages have lost a great part of the impression on me they might otherwise have had.
zh: β) 既然一种应当普遍地面向人民的宗教不可能由普遍真理构成——这些真理任何时候都只有比较杰出的人才达到，并且怀着爱和整个心去把握它们——所以总是一部分要掺进一些只能凭信赖和信仰接受的附加物，或者在它们要被人理解、要对感性有吸引力时，把那些比较纯粹的命题粗糙化，塞进一个更感性的外壳里；一部分又必须引入一些习俗，而它们的必要性或好处，也要靠信赖的信仰或从小养成的习惯来劝说人10) ——既然如此，那么显然，民间宗教，以及（这本来就与宗教的概念本身连在一起）如果它的学说要在生活和行动中起作用，就不可能建立在单纯的理性上。—— 实证宗教必然建立在对于传统的信仰上，宗教正是通过传统传给我们，——因此，对于它的宗教习俗，我们也只能凭这个根据才相信我们有义务遵守它们，才相信上帝把它们当作可喜的、当作义务向我们要求。
但若只就本身用理性来考察，关于它们能断言的至多只是：它们有助于感化，有助于唤起虔诚的感受；而它们在这方面的合目的性是可以考察的。
可是，一旦我确信上帝本身并不通过这些习俗、通过我们的侍奉而受到敬奉，确信行正道才是他最喜爱的侍奉，而我又看出这些习俗确实有助于感化，那么恰恰因此，这些习俗在我身上就失去了它们本来可能有的很大一部分印象。

en: Just as religion in general is a matter of the heart, so it could be a question how far reasoning may mix in, in order to remain religion.

If one reflects much on the origin of the feelings, on the usages one has to join in and through which pious feelings are to be awakened, on their historical origin, on their appropriateness and the like, then they certainly lose something of the nimbus of holiness with which we were always accustomed to see them, just as the dogmas of theology lose their authority when we illuminate them with church history.

But how little such cold reflection gives a man support, we often see in those who come into situations where the torn heart needs a firmer staff, where despair then often again reaches for what once gave it comfort and now clutches it all the more firmly and anxiously so that it may not slip away from it again, and deliberately stops its ear against the sophistries of the understanding.
zh: 宗教本来就是心里的事，那么推理议论可以插进多深而仍不失为宗教，这倒可以成为一个问题。
人要是对感受的产生、对自己不得不参加的、据说能唤起虔诚情感的那些习俗，对它们的历史来源、它们的合目的性等等想得很多，那么它们肯定会失去我们一向习惯于看它们时带着的那圈神圣的光晕，就像神学的教条一经用教会史来照亮，就失去了自己的威望一样。
但这样一种冷静的思索给人多么少的支撑，我们常常在这样的人身上看到：他们陷入某种处境，破碎的心需要一根更牢靠的手杖，绝望这时往往又去抓从前给过它安慰的东西，而且现在抓得更紧、更惶恐，生怕它又溜走，同时故意把耳朵堵起来，不听知性的那些诡辩。

en: Wisdom is something other than enlightenment, than reasoning.

But wisdom is not science - wisdom is an elevation of the soul which has raised itself, through experience joined with reflection, above dependence on opinions as on the impressions of sensuousness, and which, if it is practical wisdom, not mere self-satisfied or boastful wisdom, must necessarily be accompanied by a calm warmth, a gentle fire; it reasons little, nor has it proceeded methodo mathematica from concepts and arrived through a series of inferences, like Barbara and Barocco, at what it takes for truth, - it has not bought its conviction in the common market, where knowledge is handed out to anyone who pays properly, nor would it know how to count it back onto the table in blank coin, in the current denominations -, but speaks out of the fullness of the heart.
zh: 智慧和启蒙、和推理议论是另一回事。

但智慧不是科学——智慧是灵魂的一种提升：它靠经验连同对依附于意见、也依附于感性印象这一点的思索把自己提升了起来；而且，如果它是实践的智慧，不是那种自满或炫耀的智慧，就必然伴随着一种平静的温暖、一团柔和的火。它很少推理，也不是以几何学的方式（methodo mathematica）从概念出发、经过一连串像 Barbara 和 Barocco 那样的推论才达到它认作真理的东西；它没有在公共市场上买来自己的信念——在那里，谁付够了钱，知识就卖给谁——它也不会把知识以光亮的钱币、以通行的币种再数到桌上去；它是从心里的充实中说话的。

en: Cultivation of the understanding and its application to the objects that draw our interest to themselves, - enlightenment therefore remains a fine distinction, as does clear knowledge of duties, enlightenment about practical truths.
But they are not of such a nature that they could give man morality; in worth they fall back infinitely behind goodness and purity of the heart; with that they are properly [not] commensurable.
zh: 培养知性，并把它运用到吸引我们兴趣的对象上，——启蒙因此仍然是一种美好的长处，正如对义务的清楚认识、对实践真理的启蒙一样。
但它们的情况并不是能给人类以道德；在价值上，它们无限地落在心的善良和纯洁后面；它们和后者其实是[不]可相提并论的。

en: Cheerfulness is a main trait in the character of a well-disposed youth; if circumstances prevent him from it, so that he must withdraw more into himself, and he forms the resolve to educate himself into a virtuous man, and has not yet experience enough that books cannot make him one, then he perhaps takes Campe's Theophron in hand, in order to make these doctrines of wisdom and prudence the guideline of his life; he reads a section of it morning and evening and thinks of it the whole day - what will be the consequence?
Real perfection, perhaps?
Knowledge of human nature? Practical prudence?
To this belong years of practice and experience - but meditation on Campe and the Campean yardstick will make him sick of it within eight days!
Gloomy and anxious he goes into company, where only he is welcome who knows how to cheer it up; timidly he enjoys a pleasure that tastes only to him who is in it with a cheerful heart.

Penetrated by the feeling of his imperfection, he bows to everyone; intercourse with women does not brighten him up, because he fears there that a light touch of some girl might pour an igniting fire through his veins, and this gives him an awkward, stiff appearance - but he will not endure it long, but soon shakes off the supervision of this morose tutor and will be the better for it.
zh: 快活是一个天性良好的少年的性格里的一个主要特征；如果处境妨碍他快活，使他不得不更多地退缩到自己心里去，而他又下定决心要把自己培养成一个有德的人，同时还没有足够的经验，不知道书本并不能把他变成这样的人，那么他也许会拿起坎佩的《忒奥弗龙》，把里面那些智慧和精明的教训当作自己生活的准绳；他早晚各读一节，整天想着它——结果会怎样呢？
是现实的完善吗？
是通晓人情？是处世的精明？
这些要靠多年的练习和经验——但对坎佩的默想和那把坎佩式的尺子，不出八天就会让他厌烦透顶！
他阴沉而胆怯地走进社交圈，而在那里受欢迎的只有懂得让大家高兴起来的人；他畏畏缩缩地享受一种乐趣，而这种乐趣只有怀着快活的心参与其中的人才尝得出味道。
他满心感到自己的不完善，对谁都低头弯腰；和女人交往也不能使他开朗，因为他怕那里某个姑娘轻轻一碰，就会把一团火注入他的血管；这使他显得笨拙、拘谨——但他不会长久忍受下去，不久就会甩掉这位阴沉的家庭教师的管束，那时他会觉得好过一些。

en: If enlightenment is to accomplish what its great panegyrists give out about it, if it is to deserve its praises, then it is true wisdom; otherwise it commonly remains pseudo-wisdom, which puffs itself up and prides itself on its manners, which it imagines it has ahead of so many weak brothers.

This conceit is commonly found in most youths or men who through writings attain new insights and begin to give up their previous belief, which they had in common with most of those who were around them in this way, in which vanity often has a particularly large share.

Whoever knows how to say much about the incomprehensible stupidity of men; whoever demonstrates to one to a hair that it is the greatest folly for a people to have such a prejudice; whoever keeps throwing about the words enlightenment, knowledge of human nature, history of mankind, happiness, perfection - is nothing more than a babbler of enlightenment, a quack who offers insipid universal medicines for sale - they feed one another with bald words and overlook the holy, the delicate web of human feeling.

Everyone will perhaps hear such examples chattering around him; many a one has perhaps experienced it in himself, for in our over-written times this course of cultivation is very frequent. - If one or another through life itself learns to understand more of what previously lay in his soul only as dead capital, there still remains lying undigested in every stomach a heap of book-learning which, because the stomach has enough to do with it, prevents a healthier nourishment and lets no nourishing juices flow into the rest of the system of the body, - the bloated appearance perhaps gives the semblance of health, but in all limbs a juiceless phlegm paralyses free movement.
zh: 如果启蒙要做到它的那些大颂扬者所宣扬的事，如果它要配得上那些赞美，那它就是真正的智慧；否则它多半只是假智慧，自吹自擂，还为自己那些派头得意——它自以为在那么多软弱的弟兄面前有这些派头。
这种自负多半出现在大多数青年或男子身上：他们通过书本得到新的见识，开始放弃自己以前的信仰——那信仰是他们和身边大多数这样的人共有的——其中虚荣心往往起了特别大的作用。
谁要是很会大谈人有多么不可理解的愚蠢；谁能一毫不差地向人证明，一个民族抱有这样一种偏见是最大的蠢事；谁要是老把启蒙、人情世故、人类史、幸福、完善这些词挂在嘴边——他就不过是个启蒙的饶舌者，一个叫卖淡而无味的万灵药的江湖郎中；他们彼此用干巴巴的词句互相喂食，却看不见人的感受那神圣而细密的织体。

每个人也许都会听见身边有人这样叽叽喳喳地举例子；有些人也许在自己身上就体验过，因为在我们这个写得过多的时代，这种教养的路子非常常见。——如果有一两个人靠生活本身，对以前只作为死资本躺在自己灵魂里的东西也多懂了一些，那么每个胃里总还是剩下一堆没有消化的书本学问；胃为了对付它已经够忙，于是挡住更有益的食物，也不让有营养的汁液流到身体其余的系统里去；——那胀大的外表也许给人健康的假象，但一种没有汁液的黏液却在四肢里使自由的活动瘫痪下来。

en: It is a business of the enlightening understanding to sift objective religion.

But just as the power [of this understanding] is no great moment when the improvement of men, their upbringing to great strong dispositions, to noble feelings, to a resolute independence is to be produced, so too the product, objective religion, has no great weight in this.
zh: 把客观宗教加以清理甄别，是启蒙的知性的一项工作。
不过，正像在要促成人的改善、要把人培养成宏大坚强的意向、高尚的情感、果断的独立自主时，[这种知性的]力量并不是什么重要的环节，它的产物即客观宗教在这件事上也没有多大的分量。

en: It flatters the human understanding when it contemplates its work - a great high building of the knowledge of God and of the knowledge of human duties and of nature.

The building material, the materials, it has indeed procured for this; out of them it has made a building, and keeps on beautifying it or else putting flourishes on it; but the more extensive, the more composite the building becomes on which the whole of mankind works, the less does it belong to any single individual as his own.

Whoever only copies this general building, whoever collects from it only for himself, whoever does not build in himself and out of himself his own little house to dwell in, with its roof and its timber frame, where he is wholly at home, where he has - if not worked every stone entirely from the raw - at least laid it ready and turned it about in his hands, - he is a man of the letter, he has not lived and woven himself.
zh: 当人的知性端详自己的作品——一座关于上帝的知识、关于人的义务和自然的知识的宏大高耸的建筑——时，它觉得很得意。
材料、砖瓦确实是他为此搬来的；他用它们造起一座建筑，还不断地把它修饰得更漂亮，或者在它上面添些花饰；但是，这座全人类都在动手的建筑越是庞大、越是复杂，它就越不属于任何单个的人自己。
谁只是临摹这座公共建筑，只是从它那里为自己收集，谁不在自己心里、从自己出发为自己盖一座住进去的小屋，有屋顶有梁架，在那里他完全像在家里，那里的每一块石头，就算不是他完全从粗料凿出来的，也是他摆好、在手里翻弄过的——谁就是这样，谁就是个死抠字眼的人，他没有活出自己、织出自己。

en: Whoever merely builds himself a palace beside that great house lives in it like Louis XIV in Versailles; he scarcely knows all the chambers of his property and fills only a very small little cabinet — whereas a householder in his grandparental little house knows his way about everywhere better, and can give account and answer about every screw, every little cupboard, their use and their history. — [Recha in] Lessing's Nathan [V, 6]: Of most things I can still say how, where, why I learned it.
zh: 谁若只是靠着那座大宅给自己盖一座宫殿，住在里面就像路易十四住凡尔赛宫；他几乎认不全自己产业的所有厅堂，只填满一个小小的房间——而一个当家人住在祖父母留下的小屋里，处处都更清楚，每一颗螺丝、每一个小柜子，它们有什么用处、有什么来历，他都能说出个究竟。——[莱辛《智者纳坦》中的]雷霞[第五幕第六场]：对大多数事情，我还能说出我是怎样、在哪儿、为什么学会它的。

en: His little house, which a man can then call his own — religion must help to build it, but how much can it help him in that?
zh: 到那时人能称作自己的那座小屋，宗教必须帮着来盖，可是它在这上头能帮上多少忙呢？

en: If the difference between pure rational religion, which worships God in spirit and in truth and places his service only in virtue, and fetish belief, which believes it can make itself pleasing to God also by something other than a will good in itself, is so wide that the latter, in contrast to the former, has no value at all, that the two are of a wholly different kind, and if it is so important for mankind to lead the latter ever more towards rational religion and to drive out fetish belief, then the question arises — since a universal spiritual church remains only an ideal of reason, and since it is hardly possible that a public religion could be established which would take away every possibility of drawing fetish belief out of it — how a folk religion in general must be arranged, in order a) negatively to give as little occasion as possible for clinging to the letter and the usages, and b) positively — that the people would be led to rational religion and would gain receptivity for it.
zh: 纯粹理性宗教在精神和真理中敬拜神，把对神的侍奉只放在德性里；拜物信仰则相信还能靠某种并非自在善的意志的东西来讨神喜欢。如果这两者之间的差别如此之大，以致后者与前者的对立中毫无价值，两者完全属于不同的种类；而把后者越来越引向理性宗教、把拜物信仰排挤掉，对人类又如此重要——那么问题就是：既然一种普遍的精神教会始终只是理性的理想，而且几乎不可能建立起一种公共宗教，能把从中引出拜物信仰的一切可能都除掉，那么一种民间宗教在总体上该怎样安排，才能 a) 消极地尽量少给人借口，让人不至于死抓住字句和仪式不放，b) 积极地——使民众被引向理性宗教、对它有接受能力。

en: If in morality the idea of holiness is set up as the last height of the ethical and the last point of striving, then the objections of those who say that such an idea is not attainable by man (which those moralists themselves concede), but that besides the pure respect for the law he needs other motives relating to his sensuousness, prove not so much that man may not strive to approach that idea, even if it be into all eternity, but only that, given the crudeness and the powerful inclination to sensuousness of most men, one must often be content to bring forth mere legality, to bring forth which no purely moral motives are required (cf. Matth.

19, 16), for which they would have little sense, and that it is already a gain if only crude sensuousness is refined, if at least interest in something higher is awakened, and if instead of really animal drives feelings are awakened which are more capable of the influence of reason and come closer to the moral, or whereby it is really only possible that, when the loud clamour of sensuousness is somewhat damped, moral feelings too sprout up — in general, mere culture is already a gain; they want only this much, that it is probably not likely on this earth that mankind, or even a single man, will ever be able to do without the non-moral motives — and into our nature itself such feelings are woven, which, although not moral, not springing from respect for the law, and thus neither wholly firm and sure nor of value in themselves, and yet again deserving respect, are nevertheless amiable, hinder evil inclinations and further the best in men — of this kind are all good-natured inclinations, compassion, benevolence, friendship, etc. To this empirical character, which is enclosed within the circle of inclinations, belongs also the moral feeling, which must send its tender threads into the whole web; the basic principle of the empirical character is love, which has something analogous to reason, in that love finds itself in other men — or rather, forgetting itself, sets itself out from its existence, as it were lives, feels and acts in others — just as reason, as the principle of universally valid laws, recognizes itself again in every rational being, as a fellow citizen of an intelligible world.

The empirical character of men is indeed affected by pleasure and displeasure, but love, even if it is a pathological principle of action, is unselfish; it does not act well because it has calculated that the joys springing from its actions are purer and longer lasting than those of sensuousness or those springing from the satisfaction of some passion — so it is not the principle of refined self-love, where the I is in the end always the final purpose.
zh: 如果在道德学里把神圣性的观念当作伦理的最高峰和努力的最终目标，那么那些人的反驳——他们说这样的观念人达不到（那些道德学家自己也承认这一点），人除了对法则的纯粹敬重之外，还需要别的与他感性相关的动力——所证明的并不在于人不该努力去接近那个观念，哪怕要到千秋万世；只在于：面对大多数人的粗野和对感性的强大偏好，人们常常不得不满足于仅仅产生合法性，而合法性不需要任何纯粹道德的动力就能产生（参《马太福音》

19,16），那些动力对它也没多少意思；也在于：只要粗糙的感性变得精细一些，至少只唤起对更高东西的兴趣，只要不是真正动物式的冲动，而是唤起一些感受，这些感受更能受理性的影响、更接近道德的东西，就已经是收获了——或者说，其实只有在感性的喧嚷稍稍压低时，道德的感受才可能发芽——总之，仅仅是教养就已经是一种收获。他们只要求这么多：在这大地上，人类或某个人恐怕不太可能有一天会不需要那些非道德的动力。而且这样的感受就织在我们的天性里，它们虽然不是道德的，不是出自对法则的敬重，因此既不完全牢固可靠，本身也没有价值，却又值得敬重，可亲可爱，能阻止坏的偏好，促进人身上最好的东西——一切善良的偏好、同情、善意、友谊等等都属于这一类。在这个被围在偏好圈子里的经验性格中，也包含着道德感，它必须把细嫩的线送到整块织物里去；经验性格的基本原则是爱，爱与理性有某种类似，因为爱在别人身上找到自己，或者不如说，忘掉自己、从自己的存在里走出来，仿佛在别人身上生活、感受和行动——正如理性作为普遍有效法则的原则，在每个理性存在者身上又认出自己，作为理智世界的同胞。
人的经验性格固然会受快乐和不快的触动，但爱尽管是行动的一个病理学原则，却是无私的；它行善并不是因为算计过：由它的行为产生的快乐比感性的快乐、或比满足某种情欲产生的快乐更纯粹、更持久——所以它不是那种精致自爱的原则，在那种原则里，我最终始终是最后的目的。

en: For setting up principles empiricism is of course absolutely unfit; but when the question is how one is to work upon men, one must take them as they are and seek out all good drives and feelings, whereby, if not immediately his freedom, yet his nature can be ennobled.

In a folk religion especially it is of the greatest importance that imagination and heart do not remain unsatisfied, that the former be filled with great, pure images and in the latter the more beneficent feelings be awakened.

That both receive a good direction is all the more important in religion, whose object is so great, so sublime, where both too easily make paths for themselves or let themselves be misled — either that the heart, seduced by false representations and its own comfort, clings to external things or finds nourishment in low, falsely humble feelings and believes it is thereby serving God — or that the imagination links things as cause and effect whose succession is merely contingent, and promises itself extraordinary effects against nature.

Man is so many-sided a thing that anything can be made of him; the web of his feelings, so variously interwoven, has so many different ends that anything — if it does not work from one, it works from others — can be attached to it.

Hence he has been capable of the most foolish superstition, of the greatest hierarchical and political slavery. — To weave these fair threads of nature, in accordance with nature, into a noble band must be chiefly the business of folk religion.
zh: 要确立原则，经验主义当然根本不行；但若谈的是怎样对人起作用，那就必须把人当作他们本来的样子，去找出一切好的冲动和感受，借此即使不能直接提高他的自由，也能提升他的天性。
尤其在民间宗教里，最重要的是想象力和心不能得不到满足：前者要被伟大而纯粹的图像充满，后者里要唤起那些更有益的感受。
两者都得到好的方向，在宗教里就更加重要，因为宗教的对象如此伟大、如此崇高，两者在那里太容易自己给自己开路，或者被引上歧途——或者是心被错误的表象和自己的图方便所诱，攀附在外物上，或者在低劣的、假谦卑的感受里找到养料，还以为这是在侍奉神；——或者是想象力把先后相继纯属偶然的事物当作原因和结果连在一起，指望自然之外有非凡的效果。
人是这样一个多面的东西，从他身上什么都能造出来；他的感受织得如此纷繁复杂，有那么多线头，所以什么都能接上去——不从这一头下手，就从别的头下手。
因此他曾经能陷进最愚蠢的迷信，能受最厉害的教权统治和政治奴役。——把这些天性的美丽线头顺着天性编成一条高贵的带子，这首先是民间宗教的事。

en: Folk religion differs from private religion chiefly in that the purpose of the former is, by working powerfully on imagination and heart, to breathe into the soul in general the strength and the enthusiasm — the spirit — which is indispensable to great, to sublime virtue.

The cultivation of the individual in accordance with his character, instruction about cases of collision among duties, the particular means of furthering virtue, comfort and uplifting in individual sufferings and misfortunes must be left to private religion for formation; and that these do not qualify for a public folk religion is clear from the following:
zh: 民间宗教与私人宗教的区别主要在于：前者的目的是，通过强有力地作用于想象力和心，给灵魂整体注入那种力量和热情——那种精神，它是伟大、崇高的德性不可缺少的。
按照各人的性格来培养个人，就义务的冲突情况作教导，提供促进德性的特殊手段，在个别的痛苦和不幸中给以安慰和扶持——这些都该交给私人宗教去教养；而它们不配充当一种公共的民间宗教，从下面这点就可看出：

en: a) Instruction about cases of collision among duties; these are so manifold that I can help myself out in a way satisfactory to my conscience either only through the advice of upright and experienced men, or through the conviction that duty and virtue are the highest principle — which conviction may previously have been made firm and capable of becoming the maxim of my action by public religion: public instruction, like instruction in morals — of which above — is too dry, and it will no more be able than she [morality] to bring it about that the mind in the moment of action let itself be determined by fine casuistic rules; or an eternal scrupulosity would be produced, which is wholly contrary to the resolution and strength required for virtue.
zh: a) 关于义务冲突情况的教导；这些情况如此纷繁，我要让良心得到满足，只能靠正直而有经验的人的建议，或者靠这样一种确信：义务和德性是最高的原则——这种确信此前也许已经由公共宗教变得牢固，并能够成为我行动的准则：公共的授课，就像关于道德的授课——前面说过——太枯燥，它也和道德一样，做不到让心在行动的瞬间听从精细的决疑规则来定夺；否则就会生出没完没了的顾虑，这跟德性所需要的果断和力量完全相反。

en: b) If virtue is no product of teaching and chatter, but a plant which, though with proper tending, is yet formed out of its own drive and its own strength, then the many arts that people claim to have invented in order to bring virtue forth as in a hothouse, and where it is as it were not to be allowed to fail, do more harm to man than letting him run wild.11) Religious public instruction brings it about by its very nature that not only the understanding is enlightened about the idea of God and our relation to him, but that one also seeks to derive all other duties from the obligations we have toward God and to make those duties all the more urgent for us, to present them as all the more binding.

But this derivation has already something strained about it, something far-fetched; it is a connection in which only the understanding sees the coherence, which is often very artificial and at least does not strike the common human sense; and it is usual that the more motives one adduces for a duty, the colder one becomes toward it.
zh: b) 德性如果不是教导和空谈的产品，而是一株植物——它固然需要恰当的照料，却是靠自己的冲动和自己的力量长成的——那么人们声称发明出来的那许多手艺，想把德性像在温室里一样催出来、仿佛非成功不可，结果对人害处更大，还不如让他野生。11) 宗教的公共授课按其本性就会带来这样的结果：不只是知性在关于神的观念、我们与神的关系上得到启发，而且还设法把其他一切义务都从我们对神所负的责任中推出来，好让我们更强烈地记住那些义务，把它们说成更有约束力。
可是这种推导已经有点勉强、有点绕得太远；它是一种只有知性才看得出其关联的联系，这种关联往往十分做作，至少打动不了普通人的常识；而且通常情形是：为一项义务举出的动机越多，人对它反而越冷淡。

en: c) The only true comfort in suffering (for pains there is no comfort — to those one can only oppose strength of soul) is trust in God's providence; everything else is empty chatter that slides off the heart.
zh: c) 在苦难中唯一真正的安慰（痛苦是没有安慰的——对痛苦只能拿灵魂的力量去抵挡）是信赖神的护佑；别的都是空话，从心上滑过去。

en: How must folk religion be constituted?
(Folk religion is here taken objectively.)
zh: 民间宗教必须是什么样的？
（这里是把民间宗教客观地来看。）

en: a) With regard to the objective doctrines
zh: a) 就客观的教义而言

en: b) with regard to the ceremonies.
zh: b) 就仪式而言。

en: A. I. Its doctrines must be grounded in universal reason.
zh: A. I. 它的教义必须建立在普遍理性之上。

en: II.
Imagination, heart and sensuousness must not go away empty here.
zh: II.
想象、心和感性在这里不能空手而去。

en: III.
It must be so constituted that all the needs of life, the public acts of the state, attach themselves to it.
zh: III.
它必须这样安排：生活的一切需要、公共的国家行为都接在它上面。

en: B. What does it have to avoid?
zh: B. 它要避免什么？

en: Fetish belief — under which, especially in our word-rich age, this too is often the case, that by tirades about enlightenment and the like one
believes to have satisfied the demand of reason; that people forever squabble over dogmatic doctrines and meanwhile improve themselves or others the less.
zh: 拜物信仰——尤其是在我们这个多话的时代，还常有这样的事：人们用一通关于启蒙之类的长篇大论，
就以为自己已经满足了理性的要求；人们为教条永远争吵不休，同时却很少使自己或别人变好一点。
